label: Power BI
headline: Power BI Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Power BI — from loading data and Power Query transformations to DAX measures, chart types, and data profiling.

items.name: Power BI Desktop
items.definition: The Windows desktop application for building reports and data models. Where you connect data, write DAX, and design visuals.

items.name: Power BI Service
items.definition: Cloud-based version of Power BI. Used for report publishing, sharing, scheduling refreshes, and collaboration.

items.name: Power BI Mobile
items.definition: View and interact with published reports on the go. Supports annotations, alerts, and favorites.

items.name: Report View
items.syntax: Default view — canvas for building visuals
items.definition: The main canvas where you create, arrange, and format visualizations. Most report-building happens here.

items.name: Data View
items.syntax: Table icon in the left sidebar
items.definition: Shows the raw data tables loaded into the model. Use it to inspect values, verify data types, and review calculated columns.

items.name: Model View
items.syntax: Diagram icon in the left sidebar
items.definition: Displays all tables and their relationships. Used to create, edit, and manage how tables connect to each other.

items.name: Get Data
items.definition: Entry point for connecting to any data source — Excel, CSV, SQL Server, SharePoint, web pages, APIs, and more.

items.name: Load dataset
items.syntax: Get Data → choose source → double-click → Load
items.definition: Imports the data directly into the model without opening Power Query. Click Transform Data instead to shape data first.

items.name: Transform Data
items.definition: Opens the Power Query Editor before loading. Use this to clean, reshape, and prepare data before it enters the model.

items.name: Data view inspection
items.syntax: Click the Data View icon after loading
items.definition: After loading, click Data View to verify the data was loaded correctly — check row counts, data types, and sample values.

items.name: Refresh data
items.definition: Re-executes all queries to pull the latest data from connected sources. Scheduled refresh is configured in Power BI Service.

items.name: Create relationship
items.syntax: Model View → drag column from one table to another
items.definition: Link two tables by dragging a key column onto a matching column in another table. Defines how filters propagate between tables.

items.name: Open (on load)
items.syntax: Home tab → Get Data → Transform Data
items.definition: Opens Power Query Editor during the initial data connection flow before the data is loaded into the model.

items.name: Open (already loaded)
items.definition: Opens Power Query Editor for an already loaded dataset. All existing steps are preserved in the Applied Steps pane.

items.name: Applied Steps
items.syntax: Right pane in Power Query Editor
items.definition: Every transformation is recorded as a step. Steps can be renamed, reordered, deleted, or inspected. Click any step to see the state of the data at that point.

items.name: Remove Rows
items.syntax: Home tab → Remove Rows → choose option
items.definition: Removes rows based on position or condition: Remove Top Rows, Remove Bottom Rows, Remove Duplicates, Remove Blank Rows, Remove Errors.

items.name: Add Column
items.definition: Creates a new column using an M Code formula. Define the name and expression. The column is computed row by row.

items.name: Replace Values
items.syntax: Select column → Transform tab → Replace Values
items.definition: Find and replace a specific value with another value in the selected column.

items.name: Change Data Type
items.syntax: Click type icon in column header → select type
items.definition: Sets the column type (Whole Number, Decimal, Text, Date, DateTime, True/False, etc.). Always set types explicitly before loading.

items.name: Promote Headers
items.syntax: Home tab → Use First Row as Headers
items.definition: Converts the first data row into the column headers. Common after importing raw CSV or Excel files.

items.name: Split Column
items.syntax: Transform tab → Split Column → By Delimiter / By Number of Characters
items.definition: Splits a text column into multiple columns or rows based on a delimiter or character count.

items.name: Pivot / Unpivot
items.syntax: Select columns → Transform tab → Pivot Column / Unpivot Columns
items.definition: Pivot rotates unique values of a column into new column headers. Unpivot converts column headers back into rows.

items.name: Group By
items.definition: Aggregates data by one or more grouping columns. Equivalent to GROUP BY in SQL or SUMMARIZE in DAX.

items.name: Merge Queries
items.definition: Joins two queries on a matching key column. Select the join kind to control which rows are kept.

items.name: Append Queries
items.definition: Stacks two or more queries with the same column structure on top of each other. Equivalent to UNION ALL in SQL.

items.name: Left Outer
items.definition: All rows from the left table, with matching rows from the right. Nulls where no match exists on the right. Most common join in Power Query.

items.name: Right Outer
items.definition: All rows from the right table, with matching rows from the left. Nulls where no match exists on the left.

items.name: Full Outer
items.definition: All rows from both tables. Nulls on both sides where no match exists.

items.name: Inner
items.definition: Only rows that have a matching key in both tables. Non-matching rows are excluded entirely.

items.name: Left Anti
items.definition: Only rows from the left table that have no match in the right table. Used to find unmatched records.

items.name: Right Anti
items.definition: Only rows from the right table that have no match in the left table.

items.name: Bar Chart
items.definition: Compare specific values across categories. Best for comparing many categories or long category names. E.g. Sales by Region.

items.name: Column Chart
items.definition: Compare specific values across categories. Same as Bar Chart but vertical — better for fewer categories and time series comparisons.

items.name: Line Chart
items.definition: Show trends over time. Best for visualising a numeric value changing continuously (e.g. Revenue over time).

items.name: Area Chart
items.syntax: Line chart with area below filled in
items.definition: Same as Line Chart but emphasises the magnitude of the value. The area between the axis and line is filled.

items.name: Scatter Chart
items.definition: Display one set of values along the X axis and another set along the Y axis to show relationships or outliers (e.g. Age vs Loan amount).

items.name: Combo Chart
items.definition: Combines a column chart and a line chart in one visual. Useful for overlaying an actual value vs a target (e.g. Sales performance vs target).

items.name: Treemap
items.definition: Visualises categories as coloured rectangles sized by their value. Good for hierarchical data and part-to-whole comparisons (e.g. Product category by sales).

items.name: Pie Chart
items.definition: Shows proportions of a whole. Use sparingly — hard to read with more than 5 segments. Donut Chart is a cleaner alternative.

items.name: Donut Chart
items.definition: Same as Pie Chart but with a blank centre. Slightly easier to read and allows a centre label (e.g. total value).

items.name: Map
items.definition: Plot categorical and quantitative data on a map using latitude/longitude or place names (e.g. Sales by State).

items.name: Card
items.definition: Displays a single fact or KPI prominently — a sum, count, or any measure as a large number with a label.

items.name: Table
items.definition: Displays data in a logical series of rows and columns. Good for detailed data lookup or when exact values matter more than patterns.

items.name: Matrix
items.definition: Like a Table but supports row and column grouping — similar to a pivot table. Supports drill-down on hierarchies.

items.name: Slicer
items.definition: An on-canvas filter control that lets report viewers interactively filter other visuals by clicking values.

items.name: Add a visual
items.syntax: Report View → Visualizations pane → click a visual type
items.definition: Click any icon in the Visualizations pane to add that chart type to the canvas. Then drag fields onto it from the Fields pane.

items.name: Fields: Values vs Axis
items.definition: Drag numeric measures to Values to aggregate them. Drag dimension columns to Axis, Legend, or Rows to group by them.

items.name: Change aggregation
items.syntax: Click visual → Values pane → dropdown on field → choose SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, etc.
items.definition: Power BI automatically sums numeric fields. Change the aggregation by clicking the dropdown arrow next to the field in the Values well.

items.name: Format visual
items.definition: Control colours, fonts, borders, titles, data labels, axes, and legend. Every visual element can be customised here.

items.name: Drill down
items.syntax: Click the drill-down arrow icon on a visual
items.definition: Navigate into a hierarchy — from Year to Quarter to Month to Day — within a single visual without filtering other visuals.

items.name: Cross-filter
items.syntax: Click any bar/slice in one visual
items.definition: Clicking a data point in one visual automatically filters all other visuals on the page by that value. This is the default Power BI interaction.

items.name: New Measure
items.syntax: Home tab → New Measure (or right-click table)
items.definition: Creates a DAX measure — a formula evaluated in filter context. Measures don't add a column; they compute dynamically in each visual cell.

items.name: New Column
items.definition: Creates a calculated column — a DAX formula evaluated row by row during model refresh. Stored in the table, not computed in visuals.

items.name: SUM / AVERAGE
items.syntax:
Total Sales = SUM('sales_data'[deal_size])
Avg Deal = AVERAGE('sales_data'[deal_size])
items.definition: Aggregate a numeric column. These are the most common starting measures in any Power BI report.

items.name: COUNT / DISTINCTCOUNT
items.definition: COUNT counts non-blank values. DISTINCTCOUNT counts unique values — use it for customer counts, unique IDs, etc.

items.name: IF (conditional measure)
items.definition: Creates a conditional result. Used in calculated columns for row-level flags, or in measures for conditional aggregations.

items.name: CALCULATE (context modifier)
items.definition: The core DAX function for overriding filter context. Used in almost every non-trivial measure.

items.name: DIVIDE (safe division)
items.definition: Safe division — returns the third argument (default BLANK) instead of an error when the denominator is zero.

items.name: LEFT / LOWER / UPPER
items.definition: Text manipulation for calculated columns. LEFT extracts characters from the start; LOWER/UPPER changes case.

items.name: CALENDAR (date table)
items.definition: Generates a date table. Required for time intelligence functions to work correctly in Power BI.

items.name: WEEKDAY
items.definition: Returns the day of the week as a number. Second argument sets week start: 1=Sunday-Saturday, 2=Monday-Sunday.

items.name: TOTALYTD (time intelligence)
items.definition: Calculates a year-to-date value. Requires a proper date table with a continuous date range marked as a date table.

items.name: Enable Data Profiling
items.syntax: Power Query → View tab → tick options
items.definition: Data profiling shows quality stats below each column in Power Query Editor. Enable Column Quality, Column Distribution, and Column Profile.

items.name: Column Quality
items.definition: Shows the percentage of valid, error, and empty values for each column. Quickly spot columns with missing or problematic data.

items.name: Column Distribution
items.definition: Shows a histogram of value frequencies for each column. Reveals the spread and identifies dominant values or outliers.

items.name: Column Profile
items.syntax: View tab → Column Profile (select a column first)
items.definition: Shows detailed statistics for the selected column: distinct count, null count, min, max, average, and a value distribution chart.

items.name: Profile based on entire dataset
items.syntax: Bottom bar in Power Query → 'Column profiling based on top 1000 rows' → click to toggle
items.definition: By default, profiling samples only the first 1,000 rows. Click the status bar text to switch to profiling the entire dataset.

items.name: Error inspection
items.syntax: Click 'Errors' link in Column Quality bar
items.definition: Filters the table to show only rows with errors in that column. Helps identify the cause of type conversion or formula errors.

items.name: Publish to Service
items.definition: Uploads the .pbix file to Power BI Service. The report and dataset are published separately and can be managed independently.

items.name: Share a report
items.definition: Share a link with specific people or your organisation. Recipients need a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User licence to view shared content.

items.name: Schedule refresh
items.syntax: Power BI Service → Dataset settings → Scheduled Refresh
items.definition: Configures automatic data refresh on a schedule. Requires a gateway for on-premises sources. Up to 8 refreshes/day on Pro.

items.name: Export to PDF / PowerPoint
items.syntax: File menu → Export → PDF or PowerPoint
items.definition: Exports a snapshot of the report pages. Dynamic filtering and drill-downs are not preserved — purely for static distribution.

items.name: Embed in Teams / SharePoint
items.syntax: Power BI Service → File → Embed report → SharePoint Online or Teams
items.definition: Embed an interactive Power BI report directly inside Microsoft Teams channels or SharePoint pages without requiring a separate app.

items.name: Row-Level Security (RLS)
items.syntax: Modeling tab → Manage Roles → define DAX filter
items.definition: Restricts which rows each user sees. Define roles with DAX filter expressions, then assign users to roles in Power BI Service.
